title: Deepfaked Endorsements: When the Famous Face Is Not Real
summary: AI tools can now produce convincing video and audio of well-known people saying things they never said. Scammers use this to fabricate interviews and live streams in which a famous founder or celebrity appears to promote a giveaway or a trading platform.
blocks: AI tools can now produce convincing video and audio of well-known people saying things they never said. Scammers use this to fabricate interviews and live streams in which a famous founder or celebrity appears to promote a giveaway or a trading platform.
The fakes often run on hijacked or lookalike accounts, complete with urgency — a countdown, a limited quota, a QR code on screen. The person shown has no connection to the scheme.

Assume any video that pairs a famous face with a request to send funds or scan a code is fabricated until proven otherwise. Check the person's verified channels for any mention; genuine companies do not run promotions that require you to transfer crypto first.
